{{Plainlist| * [[Oladipo Jadesimi]] * Suzanna McQuiston }} }} '''Emma Clare Thynn, Marchioness of Bath''' (''[[Birth name|née]]'' '''McQuiston'''; born 26 March 1986), styled as '''Viscountess Weymouth''' from 2013 to 2020, is a British aristocrat, socialite, model, and television personality.{{Cite web |title=Everything You Need to Know About Britain's First Black Marchioness Emma Weymouth |url=https://www.wmagazine.com/story/emma-weymouth-british-marchioness-royal-model |access-date=2023-04-24 |website=W Magazine |date=7 November 2017 |language=en}} She is married to [[Ceawlin Thynn, 8th Marquess of Bath]] and is the first [[Black British|Black]] marchioness in the [[Peerages in the United Kingdom|British peerage]].{{cite web |last1=Rhys |first1=Gillian |title=Britain's first biracial marchioness Emma Weymouth is a billionaire oil heiress, London socialite, Strictly Come Dancing star and Vogue editor |date=1 May 2020 |url=https://www.scmp.com/magazines/style/news-trends/article/3082161/britains-first-black-marchioness-emma-weymouth |website=Style Magazine |publisher=South China Morning Post |accessdate=3 June 2020}} Thynn competed on the reality television shows ''[[Strictly Come Dancing]]'', ''[[Pointless]]'', and ''[[MasterChef (British TV series)#Celebrity MasterChef|Celebrity MasterChef]]'' before becoming a cast member on ''[[Ladies of London|Ladies of London: The New Reign]]'' in 2026. == Early life and education == Thynn was born on 26 March 1986, in London, the daughter of a Nigerian father and an English mother.{{Cite news |last=Holt |first=Bethan |date=2024-08-30 |title=Marchioness of Bath named new face of Victoria’s Secret |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/fashion/style/victorias-secret-marchioness-of-bath/ |access-date=2025-06-03 |work=The Telegraph |language=en-GB |issn=0307-1235}} Her father, Chief [[Oladipo Jadesimi]], is a Nigerian oil billionaire who is the executive chairman of [[LADOL|Lagos Deep Offshore Logistics Company]] and a titleholder in the [[Nigerian chieftaincy system]], while her mother, Suzanna McQuiston, is an English socialite.[http://investing.businessweek.com/research/stocks/people/person.asp?personId=44461994&ticker=FCMB:NL&previousCapId=22125422&previousTitle=FIRST%20CITY%20MONUMENT%20BANK%20PLC Ladi Jadesimi]{{dead link|date=April 2023|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}, business profile.Lagos Deep Offshore Logistics Base: [http://www.ladol.com/about-us/management Lagos Deep Offshore Logistics Base Management], retrieved 28 November 2017. As a result of an affair between her parents, her father did not live with the family, but she has reported having a positive relationship with him.{{Cite web |last=Curtis |first=Nick |date=2018-06-20 |title=How posh are your cakes? Meet Viscountess Weymouth, the aristo Nigella |url=https://www.thetimes.com/life-style/food-drink/article/how-posh-are-your-cakes-meet-viscountess-weymouth-the-aristo-nigella-3s89m6lqv |access-date=2025-03-07 |website=www.thetimes.com |language=en}} She has several half-siblings, including [[Amy Jadesimi]].{{cite news |last1=Marsh |first1=Stefanie |title=Britain's first black marchioness |url=https://www.thetimes.com/culture/tv-radio/article/britains-first-black-marchioness-3t7vz208g22 |website=[[The Times]] |access-date=6 December 2021}} She was raised in [[South Kensington]].{{cite magazine |last=Kamp |first=David |date=25 April 2018 |title=Meet the Viscountess Transforming the Idea of British Aristocracy |url=https://www.vanityfair.com/style/2018/04/viscountess-weymouth-emma-thynn |access-date=31 December 2018 |magazine=Vanity Fair |publisher=Condé Nast}} She was [[Head girl and head boy|head girl]] at [[Queen's Gate School]] during her secondary education and later attended [[University College London]] to study [[art history]].{{cite web |date=19 November 2015 |title=Pride & prejudice: Emma Weymouth on sleeping with Longleat's lions and beating the blue-blooded bigots |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/lifestyle/esmagazine/pride-prejudice-emma-weymouth-on-sleeping-with-longleats-lions-and-beating-the-blueblooded-bigots-a3118056.html |accessdate=29 November 2017 |website=London Evening Standard}}{{cite news |last=Ward |first=Audrey |title=A Life in the Day: Viscountess Emma Weymouth {{pipe}} The Sunday Times Magazine |url=https://www.thetimes.com/article/a-life-in-the-day-viscountess-emma-weymouth-vkx6txc2k |access-date=29 November 2017 |website=[[The Times]]}} After university, she studied classical acting at the [[London Academy of Music and Dramatic Art]].{{cite web |title=Emma McQuiston |url=https://www.huffpost.com/author/emma-mcquiston |accessdate=4 November 2019 |website=HuffPost}} == Career == After her marriage, she became [[Châtelain|chatelaine]] of Longleat's estate and safari park.{{cite news |last1=Simpson |first1=Craig |title=Viscountess Emma Weymouth: 'I want to bring everything back to Longleat - even the pineapples |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2020/11/29/viscountess-emma-weymouth-want-bring-everything-back-longleat/ |website=The Telegraph |date=29 November 2020 |access-date=7 December 2021}} There, she founded the food and lifestyle brand ''Emma's Kitchen''.{{Cite web|url=https://www.longleat.co.uk/longleat-house/emmas-kitchen|title=Emma's Kitchen|last=|first=|date=|website=Longleat|access-date=6 April 2020}} She was featured alongside her husband in ''All Change at Longleat'', a three-part documentary filmed in 2014 and broadcast on [[BBC One]] in September 2015.{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b06cxkzv|title=BBC One - All Change at Longleat|website=BBC|language=en-GB|access-date=10 August 2019}} In 2017, she became a brand ambassador for [[Fiorucci]].{{Cite web|url=http://emma-weymouth.com/emma-loves-fiorucci/|title=Emma Loves... Fiorucci|date=29 September 2017|website=Emma Weymouth|language=en-US|access-date=6 April 2020|archive-date=6 April 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200406095759/http://emma-weymouth.com/emma-loves-fiorucci/|url-status=dead}} She also modelled for [[Dolce & Gabbana]], walking in runway shows at [[Harrods]].{{cite web|url=https://www.wmagazine.com/story/emma-weymouth-british-marchioness-royal-model|title=Meet Emma Weymouth, Britain's First Black Marchioness Who Just Modeled for Dolce & Gabbana|author=Marissa G. Muller|website=W Magazine|date=7 November 2017 |accessdate=29 November 2017}} In February 2018, Thynn began working as a fashion editor at [[British Vogue|British ''Vogue'']].{{cite web|url=http://emma-weymouth.com|title=Emma Weymouth {{pipe}} Moderation Not Deprivation|website=Emma-weymouth.com|accessdate=29 November 2017}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.vogue.co.uk/profile/emma-weymouth|title=Emma Weymouth News and Features|website=British Vogue|language=en-GB|access-date=6 April 2020}} She is also contributing editor at ''[[Huffington Post|HuffPost]]''.{{cite web|url=https://www.huffpost.com/entry/back-from-the-wilderness-london-fashion-week_b_6727954|title=Back From the Wilderness – London Fashion Week|website=HuffPost|date=22 February 2015|accessdate=29 November 2017}} From September 2019, she was a contestant in the 17th series of the BBC television programme ''[[Strictly Come Dancing]]'', partnered with professional dancer [[Aljaž Škorjanec]]. The couple were eliminated in week seven. She became involved in a voting controversy after a staff member at [[Longleat|Longleat House]] offered to pay for colleagues' votes in her support.{{Cite news |last=Reporters |first=Telegraph |date=2019-10-26 |title=Emma Weymouth 'completely devastated' over Strictly Come Dancing voting scandal |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2019/10/26/emma-weymouth-completely-devastated-strictly-come-dancing-voting/ |access-date=2025-03-07 |work=The Telegraph |language=en-GB |issn=0307-1235}} On 18 September 2021, she was a contestant alongside [[Lauren Steadman]] in the "Strictly" celebrities special of ''[[Pointless]]''; her duo was the first eliminated duo of the episode.{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/m000zwyv|title = BBC One - Pointless Celebrities, Series 14, Strictly}} In 2023, Emma and her husband, [[Ceawlin Thynn, 8th Marquess of Bath]], hosted [[Prince Edward, Duke of Edinburgh]], at [[Longleat|Longleat House]]. The visit was part of the Rededication of the 43rd Wessex Division Service held at [[Longleat]], the family seat of the [[Marquess of Bath|Marquesses of Bath]]. [[Prince Edward, Duke of Edinburgh|Prince Edward]] met with the [[Ceawlin Thynn, 8th Marquess of Bath|Marquess]] and [[Marchioness of Bath]] and their two sons, John Thynn, [[Viscount Weymouth]], and Lord Henry Thynn.{{Cite web |last=Bridger-Linning |first=Stephanie |date=2023-05-19 |title=The Marchioness of Bath delivers a masterclass in regal dressing as she hosts the Duke of Edinburgh at Longleat |url=https://www.tatler.com/article/the-marchioness-of-bath-delivers-a-masterclass-in-regal-dressing-as-she-hosts-the-duke-of-edinburgh-at-longleat |access-date=2025-05-29 |website=Tatler |language=en-GB}}[[File:Séance photo dans le lobby de l’Hôtel Martinez.jpg|thumb|Thynn at a photo shoot in the lobby of the [[Hôtel Martinez]] in 2026]]In August 2024, Thynn took part in the nineteenth series of ''[[Celebrity MasterChef]]'' on BBC One, where she was eliminated in the third heat.{{cite web |title=Celebrity MasterChef 2024: Heat 3 quarter-finalists revealed as another star is eliminated |url=https://virginradio.co.uk/entertainment/155621/celebrity-masterchef-2024-heat-3-quarter-finalist-lineup |accessdate=30 August 2024 |website=virginradio.co.uk/entertainment}} The same year, Emma was announced as an ambassador for Victoria’s Secret. The campaign featuring Thynn was filmed at [[Longleat]], her family's estate in [[Wiltshire]]. Her appointment was part of the company’s broader efforts to update its brand image. In 2025, Thynn was named "Best Hostess" in [[Tatler|Tatler's]] Country House Awards.{{Cite news |last=Forbes |first=Sacha |date=June 2025 |title=The Tatler 2025 Country House Awards |work=[[Tatler]] |pages=106-109}} In 2026, Thynn joined the cast of the reality television series ''[[Ladies of London|Ladies of London: The New Reign]]'', which premiered on [[Bravo (American TV network)|Bravo]] on March 5, 2026.[https://www.tatler.com/article/the-marchioness-of-bath-is-joining-ladies-of-london-emma-thynn The Marchioness of Bath is joining ''Ladies of London''! Emma Thynn lets cameras into Longleat in the hit reality TV show] == Personal life == She met [[Ceawlin Thynn, 8th Marquess of Bath|Ceawlin]] when she was four and he was 16, at the wedding of her half-brother Iain McQuiston to Ceawlin’s aunt, Lady Silvy Cerne Thynne. Over the following two decades, they saw each other only occasionally at large family gatherings. She and Ceawlin Thynn, Viscount Weymouth married on 8 June 2013,{{cite news |title=New Longleat Exhibitions Celebrate Weddings Past and Present |url=https://www.longleat.co.uk/news/new_longleat_exhibitions_celebrate_weddings_past_and_present |access-date=3 January 2023 |publisher=Longleat Enterprises Ltd |date=21 May 2014 |quote=...A unique exhibition celebrating the recent wedding of Ceawlin Thynn, the 12th Viscount Weymouth, to Emma McQuistom has gone on display in Longleat House. The wedding, which took place on June 8th 2013, was one of the largest held at Longleat.}} in a ceremony attended by 355 guests. Upon her marriage, she became Viscountess Weymouth.{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/profiles/54qLpWzcXpl1xb84w78GHZb/viscountess-emma-weymouth|title=BBC One - Strictly Come Dancing - Viscountess Emma Weymouth|website=BBC|language=en-GB|access-date=6 April 2020}} The wedding drew attention due to the absence of her in-laws. It was reported that [[Anna Thynn, Marchioness of Bath|Lady Bath]] did not attend, with some speculating that she felt the marriage would affect the family's heritage.{{Cite web |last=Wise |first=Louise |date=2019-10-26 |title=Lady Emma Weymouth, Britain’s first black viscountess, on Strictly, diversity and life at Longleat |url=https://www.thetimes.com/culture/tv-radio/article/lady-emma-weymouth-britains-first-black-viscountess-on-strictly-diversity-and-life-at-longleat-s902wkh2j |access-date=2025-03-07 |website=www.thetimes.com |language=en}} Emma Thynn, Marchioness of Bath, and her husband Ceawlin Thynn, 8th Marquess of Bath, have two sons, John Alexander Ladi Thynn (born 2014, heir apparent) and Henry Richard Isaac Thynn (born 2016), whose godmother is [[Lady Kitty Spencer]], niece of [[Diana, Princess of Wales]].[https://www.tatler.com/article/who-is-emma-thynn-ladies-of-london Who is Emma Thynn, the Marchioness of Bath? Meet the chatelaine of Longleat set to star in ''Ladies of London''] In 2016, Emma became the first member of the British aristocracy to have a child via [[surrogacy]] after medical advice indicated potential health risks associated with pregnancy; her second son was delivered at a private clinic in the United States. The couple opted for surrogacy after Emma was diagnosed with a brain bleed and a pituitary gland disorder during her first pregnancy. The condition caused significant pain and led to the baby being delivered by [[Caesarean section|caesarean]] section. Medical professionals advised that a second pregnancy could pose serious health risks.{{Cite news |last=Harley |first=Nicola |date=2017-01-07 |title=Longleat heir has son born by surrogacy after medics warned pregnancy could kill Lady Weymouth |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2017/01/07/longleat-heir-has-son-born-surrogacy-first-british-aristocracy/ |access-date=2025-03-07 |work=The Telegraph |language=en-GB |issn=0307-1235}} When her husband succeeded his [[Alexander Thynn, 7th Marquess of Bath|father]] as the [[Marquess of Bath]] in 2020, she became the first biracial marchioness in British history.{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/uknews/10250518/Britains-first-black-viscountesss-regret-over-father-in-laws-wedding-snub.html|title=Britain's first black viscountess's regret over father-in-law's wedding snub|website=Telegraph|accessdate=29 November 2017|date=18 August 2013|last1=Bryant|first1=Ben}}{{cite web|url=http://solarey.net/viscountess-weymouth-emma-mcquiston-britains-first-black-marchioness/|title=Viscountess Weymouth: Emma McQuiston – Britain's first black Marchioness|website=Sola Rey|accessdate=29 November 2017|date=23 February 2015}}{{cite web|url=https://abcnews.go.com/Entertainment/inside-glamorous-life-britains-black-marchioness/story?id=21235642|title=Inside the Glamorous extract: Emma Clare Thynn, Marchioness of Bath (née McQuiston; born 26 March 1986), styled as Viscountess Weymouth from 2013 to 2020, is a British aristocrat, socialite, model, and television personality. She is married to Ceawlin Thynn, 8th Marquess of Bath and is the first Black marchioness in the British peerage. Thynn competed on the reality television shows Strictly Come Dancing, Pointless, and Celebrity MasterChef before becoming a cast member on Ladies of London: The New Reign in 2026.
